summary:
The existing C2 failure collector can retain one unambiguous final failing public verify tuple as exact command/input/owner bytes with sizes and SHA256, joined to the final copied lane log. It considers only fixed Provider/Runner attempt names, reuses the existing public-profile shape checks, and refuses missing, changed, duplicate, private, unknown, sensitive or incoherent data. Exact bytes are not redacted and then called exact: the whole optional tuple is omitted instead. Original cause, reported cleanup and emitted client/server logs take priority over metadata. The selected reporter keeps its existing 96 KiB whole-report, 2-second collection, 3-second outer reporting, 16-file and 128-entry limits; metadata has 32/8/8 KiB raw subcaps and a 68 KiB serialized-frame cap. Closed nested producer fields refuse arbitrary environment or unknown records. The final tuple must join the adapter status, including timeout 124, and any partial later attempt refuses even if its log matches an earlier one. Previously retained file names count once; extra lookups consume the remaining allowance. All-or-nothing tuple admission with complete:false omission never renews a command deadline or changes original exit, retirement, model-checking or retry decisions. Recorded input times are diagnostic shape data rather than fresh launch authority; complete retained counterparts still do not establish current pin/alias checks or retry eligibility. Public synthetic file/JSON controls exercise exact recovery after scratch removal, superseded attempts, privacy/coherence/refusal and budget/error preservation. This is source-boundary knowledge, not formal or installed runtime qualification. A separate client limitation remains: the cited Quint 0.32.0 release-tag TLC path drops a compile-failure explanation before its generic CLI error. Retention preserves emitted evidence but cannot recover text never emitted. That source observation is not proof of the deployed binary build or a particular gRPC/protobuf failure cause; a corrected client artifact and provenance/pin transition require separate owning admission.

Current owner-receipt evolution must be checked at the actual producer boundary. The shared owner adds absoluteRetirementDeadline, detachedDomainEvidence and detachedDomainScope even when the C2 caller selects no detached domain. An older closed field census therefore rejected current authentic receipts and omitted the optional exact diagnostic tuple. The guard now accepts either the unchanged legacy census or the complete current census, with a null or finite positive retirement deadline and both detached fields strictly null. Non-null detached data, partial/unknown fields and malformed numeric values still refuse; original byte/frame/privacy limits remain. A causal source control invokes the actual receipt producer on an injected pre-birth launch failure, then verifies exact-byte retention and malformed/current-shape refusals. Forty affected command-interface controls pass. This repairs diagnostic compatibility only: it changes no command budget, retry class, first-cause classification or formal acceptance. A provider lane has its own150-second command clock, independent of earlier canonical Q1/Q2 timing; neither absent counterexamples nor later successful shards establish why a compilation stalled.
title: Retain complete public C2 diagnostic counterparts without granting retry authority
